_readme: One amazon.com pick per US guide (content/guides/*.json with kind 'spoke' and no locale; the 4 pillars and the 7 en-CA guides are excluded). One page = one store: these pages link amazon.com only, never amazon.ca. Fields: label (what the product is for, shown on the page), name (generic product type, shown), search (amazon.com search words), basis (where the page itself recommends or uses this product type; for review only, not shown). Rules followed: the page must already support the pick; nothing the page warns against; pesticides only as the generic type the page names and recommends; repellent actives only as the page names them, permethrin for clothing only; no traps, poisons or handling tools for wildlife or snakes; bite pages carry only items the page names from its medical sources. Where a page recommends nothing to buy, the pick is a neutral identification or monitoring aid from the page's own method, and the basis says so. Generic types only: no brands, prices, ratings or claims. Picks chosen October 20, 2026.

_noPick._why: US guides deliberately left without a pick after the independent check (Oct 20, 2026): the page recommends nothing a search could safely find.
_noPick.bullet-ants: The page recommends nothing to buy and never mentions a light; the headlamp support was a stretch.
_noPick.does-lysol-kill-bed-bugs: No container is named; the only product the page endorses is a registered bed bug pesticide, unsafe as a search.
_noPick.zombie-ants: Page never mentions a magnifier; its own check is photos with a coin for scale. It recommends nothing to buy.
_noPick.black-widow-bite: Emergency and medical page (call 911 or Poison Control); nothing to buy belongs on it.
_noPick.wasp-nest-identification: The page recommends nothing a search could safely find (no removal products by design).

alaska-mosquitoes.label: To shield face and neck
alaska-mosquitoes.name: Mosquito head net
alaska-mosquitoes.basis: 'How should you protect yourself from mosquitoes in Alaska?': the National Park Service's advice for Brooks Range visitors lists head nets, bug coats, long pants and insect repellents; list item 'Head net and bug coat. The park service names both, and recommends pairing them with a billed cap.'

animal-droppings.label: For droppings cleanup
animal-droppings.name: Disposable gloves
animal-droppings.basis: 'How do you clean up animal droppings safely?': CDC rodent steps 'wear rubber or plastic gloves'; raccoon latrines: 'CDC's steps are disposable gloves, scrubbable boots or disposable booties'

animals-in-attic.label: For raccoon latrine cleanup
animals-in-attic.name: N95 respirator mask
animals-in-attic.basis: 'Are animals in the attic a health risk?': for raccoon latrines, 'CDC says to wear disposable gloves and, in a confined space such as an attic, an N95-rated respirator'

ant-killer-recipes.label: To keep bait enclosed
ant-killer-recipes.name: Refillable ant bait stations
ant-killer-recipes.basis: The page's recipes go in an enclosed station: 'use an enclosed station, not the open bottle caps the guide pictures'; recipe card 'Station: small lidded container ... out of reach of children and pets'; FAQ on outdoor use: the University of California describes liquid borate bait 'in refillable bait stations'. Empty stations only; no pesticide picked.

aphid-control-guide.label: When a spray is needed
aphid-control-guide.name: Insecticidal soap concentrate
aphid-control-guide.basis: Quick answer: spray insecticidal soap or neem oil only if water, pruning and natural enemies are not enough, and UC calls soaps and oils the best choices when a spray is needed; FAQ 'Can I use dish soap and water to kill aphids?': extension sources steer gardeners to a commercial insecticidal soap; recipe uses concentrate (potassium salts of fatty acids) at 1 to 2 percent.

are-mice-nocturnal.label: To trap night-active mice
are-mice-nocturnal.name: Mouse snap traps
are-mice-nocturnal.basis: 'When should you set and check mouse traps?': CDC says to put the baited end of a snap trap next to the wall so it forms a T, and Nebraska Extension's rough guide is two dozen snap traps for a new infestation; the page notes CDC advises against glue and live traps. Quick answer bullet: CDC says to check traps daily.

are-mosquitoes-attracted-to-light.label: For porch and patio lights
are-mosquitoes-attracted-to-light.name: Yellow incandescent bug light bulbs
are-mosquitoes-attracted-to-light.basis: 'Do yellow or LED bulbs help keep mosquitoes away?': yellow bug lights are 'the one bulb change the sources support'; EPA says they tend to attract fewer mosquitoes than ordinary lights but are not repellents, and the AMCA wording is about incandescent bulbs (LEDs untested), hence incandescent. The page says a bulb does not stand in for repellent, clothing or screens.

army-ants.label: To seal slab cracks
army-ants.name: Concrete crack filler
army-ants.basis: 'What should you do if army ants turn up in a house?': after the colony moves on, the University of Tennessee advice is to 'repair cracks in the foundation or slab and do other pest-proofing so the ants cannot return'. The page recommends no product for the ants themselves (leave them, avoid contact).

asian-lady-beetles.label: To vacuum up clusters
asian-lady-beetles.name: Wet/dry shop vacuum
asian-lady-beetles.basis: 'How do you get rid of Asian lady beetles in the house?': 'Ohio State recommends a fan-bypass vacuum such as a shop vacuum, not a direct-fan machine'; Penn State calls vacuuming the most efficient way to remove clusters; FAQ: beetles already inside are best removed with a vacuum. Foggers are ruled out.

baby-mice.label: For nest cleanup
baby-mice.name: Disposable gloves
baby-mice.basis: 'What should you do about a nest of baby mice?': 'Clean the nest up with gloves and disinfectant, without sweeping or vacuuming'; step 'Put on rubber or plastic gloves'; wash gloved hands before taking the gloves off (CDC).

bat-poop.label: For testing and cleanup
bat-poop.name: Disposable gloves
bat-poop.basis: Quick answer: the USFWS crumble test separates bat from mouse droppings, 'Do it with gloves on'; BCI's version is to squish a dropping while wearing gloves; 'How do you clean up bat droppings safely?': in rubber or plastic gloves, spray droppings with an EPA-registered disinfectant or bleach solution (CDC). Nothing for the bats themselves is picked: the page cites New Jersey law against harassing, capturing or killing bats, and NIOSH says ultrasonic devices and repellents do not work.

bed-bug-poop.label: To seal the mattress
bed-bug-poop.name: Bed bug mattress encasement
bed-bug-poop.basis: 'Can you wash bed bug poop stains out?' and FAQ 'Do you have to throw out a mattress with bed bug stains?': Cornell advises a bed bug-proof encasement on the mattress and box spring, kept on for a year and a half, which starves the bugs inside and makes new bugs easier to see.

bed-bugs-on-mattress.label: To encase the mattress
bed-bugs-on-mattress.name: Bed bug mattress encasement
bed-bugs-on-mattress.basis: Quick answer and HowTo step 'Encase the mattress and box spring': zip both into bed-bug-proof encasements and leave the covers on for a year (EPA); Texas A&M describes an encasement with a zipper tight enough to hold in the smallest life stages, woven so bugs cannot bite through.

beetles-in-house.label: To catch and check one
beetles-in-house.name: Clear specimen jars with lids
beetles-in-house.basis: 'How do you tell which beetle you have?': 'Once you know it is a beetle, catch it in a jar and run these checks'; callout: seal the beetle in a small jar, photograph it beside a ruler and note where and when you found it. Identification aid from the page's own method.

black-ants.label: To reach the colony
black-ants.name: Ant bait stations
black-ants.basis: 'What does each kind of black ant need?': small black ants need their trail removed and 'a slow-acting bait they will carry home'; table rows for the little black ant and odorous house ant both call for bait; FAQ 'Why do I suddenly see black ants in my kitchen?': bait is what reaches the colony.

black-bed-bugs.label: To check the bug's build
black-bed-bugs.name: Hand lens magnifier
black-bed-bugs.basis: 'How do you confirm whether it is a bed bug?': 'Check the build under a hand lens'; the Connecticut poster's inspection kit includes a bright flashlight, a hand lens, soft tweezers and a glass bottle; bat bugs can only be separated from bed bugs under magnification.

black-spiders.label: For work where widows live
black-spiders.name: Work gloves
black-spiders.basis: 'What should you do once you know what it is?': where widows are common, the Army fact sheet advises shaking out clothing and shoes and wearing gloves, long sleeves and boots when working where widows live, and clearing debris, lumber and rock piles from around the foundation.

borax-for-ants.label: For a weak liquid bait
borax-for-ants.name: Refillable ant bait stations
borax-for-ants.basis: 'Which ready-made ant baits contain borax or boric acid?': 'For a weaker liquid bait there are refillable stations', and the University of California calls reusable stations more useful than prepackaged baits for difficult ant problems; its recipe is applied 'in refillable, reusable bait stations'. Empty stations only; no pesticide picked.

brown-recluse-bite.label: To monitor for recluses
brown-recluse-bite.name: Spider sticky traps
brown-recluse-bite.basis: 'How do you avoid brown recluse bites?': 'Poison Control suggests making noise before entering basements, attics and storage areas, cutting clutter and using glue traps.' No treatment product picked; for a bite the page says to wash it and call Poison Control or get medical care.

brown-recluse-look-alikes.label: To count the eyes
brown-recluse-look-alikes.name: Magnifying glass
brown-recluse-look-alikes.basis: 'How do you check a spider you have caught?': trap it under a jar and 'Count them with a magnifying glass' (six eyes in three pairs means a recluse); Vetter says minor magnification shows the pattern; FAQ 'Who can confirm...': someone trained to check the eyes under magnification.

bug-bites.label: To save a caught biter
bug-bites.name: Clear specimen jars with lids
bug-bites.basis: The page recommends nothing to buy for the bite itself. Neutral identification aid from its own method, 'What if you still cannot tell what bit you?': 'If you find the insect, seal it in a jar and note where and when you found it'; UC IPM advises saving any biter you catch for identification.

bugs-in-house-in-winter.label: To seal gaps before fall
bugs-in-house-in-winter.name: Exterior caulk
bugs-in-house-in-winter.basis: 'What should you do once you know what it is?': 'Vacuum up the overwintering bugs, seal the gaps before next fall'; for western conifer seed bugs Penn State says to replace loose screens and caulk gaps around door and window frames, soffits and chimneys; quick-ID table: seal gaps before next fall. Indoor sprays and foggers are not recommended.

bugs-that-look-like-bed-bugs.label: To send one for ID
bugs-that-look-like-bed-bugs.name: Small specimen vials
bugs-that-look-like-bed-bugs.basis: 'How do you get a specimen identified by an extension office?': catch the bug, keep it intact in a small container and take or send it to the extension office; Wisconsin's lab accepts a dry hard-bodied insect 'in a small clean vial or box'; the Connecticut kit includes a glass bottle to hold insects.

bugs-that-look-like-cockroaches.label: To catch one and compare
bugs-that-look-like-cockroaches.name: Sticky insect monitoring traps
bugs-that-look-like-cockroaches.basis: 'What should you do once you know what it is?': 'If you are still not sure what you have, a sticky trap can hold a specimen to compare against the table above'; Texas A&M describes sticky cards as trapping cockroaches and other crawling insects and as most useful for monitoring.

bugs-that-look-like-fleas.label: To check it up close
bugs-that-look-like-fleas.name: Magnifying glass
bugs-that-look-like-fleas.basis: 'How can you identify the bug in a jar?': 'Catch one first in a clear jar, a sealed plastic bag or on clear tape, and use a magnifying glass'; the cat flea's combs and the bat bug's fringe hairs show only under magnification.

can-cockroaches-fly.label: To close door gaps
can-cockroaches-fly.name: Door sweep
can-cockroaches-fly.basis: 'How do you keep flying cockroaches out of the house?': keep screens and door seals tight; 'The University of California guide adds door sweeps and weather stripping'; the University of Florida advises keeping doors shut and caulking gaps around door and window frames.

can-mice-climb-walls.label: To cover larger holes
can-mice-climb-walls.name: 1/4-inch galvanized hardware cloth
can-mice-climb-walls.basis: 'What does climbing ability mean for sealing a house?': table row Larger holes, 'for mice, 24-gauge hardware cloth with 1/4 by 1/4 inch mesh' (Nebraska)

cockroach-droppings.label: To check for live roaches
cockroach-droppings.name: Cockroach sticky traps
cockroach-droppings.basis: FAQ 'Does roach poop mean an infestation?': 'Set sticky traps near the droppings and check them daily for several days'; FAQ 'What should you do when you see cockroach poop?': set sticky traps where floors meet walls near the droppings; 'How much roach poop means a big infestation?': sticky traps tell you which it is.

cockroach-eggs.label: To monitor after cleanup
cockroach-eggs.name: Cockroach sticky traps
cockroach-eggs.basis: 'What should you do with cockroach egg cases you find?': remove them, then 'Set sticky traps'; Rutgers advises follow-up until no cockroaches have been seen or caught in sticky traps for at least a month; FAQ 'Do bug sprays kill cockroach eggs?': the guides pair treatment with monitoring by sticky traps.

commercial-pest-control.label: For indoor flies
commercial-pest-control.name: Insect light trap for flies
commercial-pest-control.basis: 'What does a commercial IPM program include?': in EPA's model IPM contract 'light traps are the standard method for indoor flies'; Food Code section 6-202.13 covers insect light traps; the contract section says insect light traps are left out of the contractor's work unless requested, so the business may supply them.

deer-mice.label: To trap deer mice
deer-mice.name: Mouse snap traps
deer-mice.basis: Quick answer: 'Seal gaps larger than 1/4 inch, trap with snap traps'; 'How do you get rid of deer mice that are already inside?': trap them with snap traps while you seal, and skip glue boards, live traps and poison bait; CDC calls for spring-loaded traps that kill.

diy-pest-control.label: For mixing and applying pesticides
diy-pest-control.name: Chemical-resistant nitrile gloves
diy-pest-control.basis: 'What protective equipment do you need?': 'at a minimum chemical-resistant gloves'; UC IPM 'adds that chemical-resistant gloves are made of nitrile, neoprene, butyl or rubber'

do-ants-bite.label: For the itch
do-ants-bite.name: Anti-itch cream
do-ants-bite.basis: 'How do you treat an ant bite or sting at home?': 'Try not to scratch. Ohio State's report on pavement ant stings says frequent washing and an anti-itch cream can help avoid scratching and secondary infections.' The page sends severe reactions to emergency care.

do-carpenter-ants-bite.label: For the itch
do-carpenter-ants-bite.name: Anti-itch cream
do-carpenter-ants-bite.basis: 'How do you treat a carpenter ant bite?': MedlinePlus first aid on the page: wash the bite, ice it, and 'If necessary, take an antihistamine or apply a cream that reduces itching, following the package directions.'

do-chickens-eat-ticks.label: To clear leaf litter
do-chickens-eat-ticks.name: Leaf rake
do-chickens-eat-ticks.basis: 'What actually reduces ticks in a yard?': CDC lists removing leaf litter, clearing tall grass and brush and mowing often; the Connecticut handbook says removing leaf litter has been shown to reduce blacklegged tick nymphs on some properties. No pesticide picked (the page says to check labels before treating where birds range).

do-cockroaches-bite.label: For the itch
do-cockroaches-bite.name: Anti-itch cream
do-cockroaches-bite.basis: 'What should you do about a suspected cockroach bite?': MedlinePlus first aid steps on the page: wash the site, ice it, and 'If necessary, take an antihistamine or apply a cream that reduces itching'; follow the label directions on any medicine.

do-mosquitoes-bite-dogs.label: For time in the backyard
do-mosquitoes-bite-dogs.name: Outdoor patio fan
do-mosquitoes-bite-dogs.basis: 'How do you cut down mosquitoes around a dog's yard?': 'Run a fan. The guidelines call fan-generated wind a practical way to protect people and pets in a backyard' (American Heartworm Society guidelines). Heartworm preventives are prescription-only and dog spot-ons were not picked.

do-mothballs-keep-mice-away.label: To seal gaps instead
do-mothballs-keep-mice-away.name: Copper mesh for gaps
do-mothballs-keep-mice-away.basis: 'What works instead of mothballs?': 'Push metal mesh into gaps, or pack them with size 00 steel wool or copper mesh and caulk over it'; quick answer bullet: NC State says gaps of 1/4 inch or larger let adult mice in, so the fix is sealing those gaps and setting snap traps.

does-alcohol-kill-bed-bugs.label: To seal the mattress
does-alcohol-kill-bed-bugs.name: Bed bug mattress encasement
does-alcohol-kill-bed-bugs.basis: 'What works better than alcohol for bed bugs?': EPA recommends covers that seal mattresses and box springs so the bugs are trapped inside and die; 'What should you do if you already sprayed alcohol?': 'Move to the methods above, starting with encasements and heat'.

does-vinegar-kill-ants.label: To reach the colony
does-vinegar-kill-ants.name: Ant bait stations
does-vinegar-kill-ants.basis: Quick answer: 'Bait that workers carry home is what ends the problem'; FAQ 'What should I do if ants keep coming back after I use vinegar?': the University of California suggests putting out bait stations or gel bait at entry points; keep vinegar away from the bait.

fall-mouse-proofing-checklist.label: To plug pipe gaps
fall-mouse-proofing-checklist.name: Stainless steel wool
fall-mouse-proofing-checklist.basis: HowTo step 'Plug small holes with metal wool and caulk': 'Wedge copper or stainless steel wool tightly into each small hole around pipes and cables, then put caulk around it'; quick answer bullet: coarse steel wool is a temporary plug that rusts, and Nebraska names copper or stainless steel wool for gaps under 3/4 inch.

field-mice.label: To trap field mice
field-mice.name: Mouse snap traps
field-mice.basis: 'How is controlling field mice different from controlling house mice?': 'The core steps are the same, which are sealing openings and trapping with snap traps'; table: snap traps for deer and white-footed mice, standard mouse snap traps for voles; avoid glue boards for deer mice.

flea-eggs.label: To see eggs and specks
flea-eggs.name: Magnifying glass
flea-eggs.basis: 'What do flea eggs look like?': 'A magnifying glass shows the smooth, pearly oval, unlike a flat flake of skin'; 'How do you tell flea eggs from dandruff, flea dirt and sand?': with a magnifying glass, white ovals suggest eggs; FAQ: a dark surface and a magnifying glass help.

flies-in-house.label: For flies that remain
flies-in-house.name: Sticky fly paper ribbons
flies-in-house.basis: 'How do you get rid of the flies once you know the source?': 'A flyswatter handles a few flies, and sticky flypaper works in a confined space, hung out of reach of children and pets'; FAQ 'How do I get rid of lots of flies in my house?': a flyswatter, flypaper or an indoor light trap handles the adults that remain.

flying-ants-vs-termites.label: To check antennae and wings
flying-ants-vs-termites.name: Magnifying glass
flying-ants-vs-termites.basis: 'How can you tell a flying ant from a termite swarmer?': 'A magnifying glass, or a phone camera zoomed in on one insect, makes all three features easier to see' (elbowed or straight antennae, waist, wing lengths). The page sends termites to a licensed professional.

flying-ants.label: To get them identified
flying-ants.name: Small specimen vials
flying-ants.basis: 'What should you do about flying ants in the house?': confirm what they are; 'Texas A&M suggests collecting ants with a cotton swab dipped in rubbing alcohol and putting them in an alcohol-filled vial for a county Extension agent to identify'.

german-cockroaches.label: To bait where they hide
german-cockroaches.name: Cockroach gel bait
german-cockroaches.basis: Quick answer: Rutgers rates bait as the most effective treatment and does not recommend foggers; 'What gets rid of German cockroaches?': find them with sticky traps, take away food and water, 'place gel bait where they hide'; in the NC State study, gel-baited homes fell sharply while foggers produced no drop.

ghost-ants.label: To bait ghost ant trails
ghost-ants.name: Liquid ant bait stations
ghost-ants.basis: 'How do you get rid of ghost ants?': find the trails and 'put a sweet bait on them'; the University of Florida says sweet baits are effective for many sweet-feeding ants and that baits come as granules, liquids, gels and tamper-resistant stations; keep sprays away from the bait.

holes-in-yard.label: To measure the hole
holes-in-yard.name: Ruler marked in inches
holes-in-yard.basis: The page recommends nothing to buy (most holes need no action; ultrasonic devices, mothballs and live trapping are ruled out). Neutral identification aid from its own method: 'Lay a ruler or a coin across the opening'; callout 'Record the hole': photograph the hole beside a ruler or a coin.

honeypot-ants.label: For ants on the counter
honeypot-ants.name: Ant bait stations
honeypot-ants.basis: The page recommends nothing for honeypot ants, which it says are not household pests. Its section 'Are honeypot ants dangerous, and are they a household pest?' says ants on a kitchen counter are far more likely a common household species and points to why 'baiting beats spraying for indoor ants'. The pick is for those ants only.

house-centipedes.label: To dry out the basement
house-centipedes.name: Dehumidifier
house-centipedes.basis: Quick answer: extension services put drying out damp areas and sealing cracks ahead of spraying; 'How do you get rid of house centipedes?': 'Penn State recommends dehumidifiers and grading the soil so water drains away from the foundation'; UC IPM says using pesticides labeled for centipedes is rarely justified.

house-spiders.label: To see where spiders roam
house-spiders.name: Spider sticky traps
house-spiders.basis: 'What should you do once you know what it is?': 'Sticky traps along walls and under furniture show where spiders are active, UMN says; UC IPM says to place them where pets and children cannot reach.'

houseplant-bugs.label: To spot tiny plant pests
houseplant-bugs.name: 10x hand lens
houseplant-bugs.basis: Quick answer: 'University of Minnesota Extension suggests a 10-power hand lens, since some are very small'; 'How do you tell which bug is on your plant?': look for the sign first and the bug second, with a 10-power hand lens or a phone magnifier app.

how-long-do-ants-live.label: For ants in the house
how-long-do-ants-live.name: Ant bait stations
how-long-do-ants-live.basis: 'What does ant lifespan mean for ants in your house?': spraying kills replaceable workers while the queen keeps laying; 'That is the reasoning behind baiting. The Missouri publication says bait is passed around to other workers, larvae and queens, so it reaches ants that never leave the nest.'

how-long-do-mice-live.label: To trap mice inside
how-long-do-mice-live.name: Mouse snap traps
how-long-do-mice-live.basis: 'Will a mouse problem go away on its own?': no; UC IPM says an infestation almost always also needs population reduction, including traps, and that traps with a wide trigger plate have higher catch rates; list step 'Trap what is already inside'.

how-many-ants-are-in-the-world.label: For ants in the kitchen
how-many-ants-are-in-the-world.name: Ant bait stations
how-many-ants-are-in-the-world.basis: The page recommends nothing to buy for its main topic. Its section 'What does the global count mean for ants in your house?' says the count means little for one home and, for ants in the kitchen, points to 'a guide to controlling household ants with bait'. The pick is for household ants only.

how-much-is-pest-control.label: To monitor crawling insects
how-much-is-pest-control.name: Sticky insect monitoring traps
how-much-is-pest-control.basis: The page is about prices and recommends nothing to buy. Neutral monitoring aid from its own evidence, 'When is professional pest control worth the money?': the integrated program it describes used sticky traps to monitor cockroaches, 24-hour sticky trap catches measured which program worked, and it suggests asking whether a plan includes monitoring.

how-to-get-rid-of-ants-in-the-house.label: To bait the colony
how-to-get-rid-of-ants-in-the-house.name: Ant bait stations
how-to-get-rid-of-ants-in-the-house.basis: Quick answer: seal the gap, 'then set slow-acting bait near the trail and leave the ants feeding on it alone'; HowTo step 'Place the stations safely': set enclosed stations near trails and entry points, outdoors where you can, out of reach of children and pets; UC IPM calls baits more effective and safer than sprays.

how-to-get-rid-of-ants-in-the-kitchen.label: To keep food sealed
how-to-get-rid-of-ants-in-the-kitchen.name: Airtight food storage containers
how-to-get-rid-of-ants-in-the-kitchen.basis: 'How should you store food so ants lose interest?': 'The EPA's Citizen's Guide to Pest Control and Pesticide Safety recommends sealed glass or plastic containers'; HowTo step 'Remove food and water': move sugar, syrup, honey and pet food into closed containers. The page baits only if ants keep coming.

how-to-get-rid-of-bed-bugs.label: To monitor for bed bugs
how-to-get-rid-of-bed-bugs.name: Bed bug interceptor cups
how-to-get-rid-of-bed-bugs.basis: Quick answer: check interceptor traps weekly; HowTo step 'Install interceptors and inspect weekly': place an interceptor trap under each leg of the bed and nearby furniture and inspect at least every 7 days; FAQ 'Should I sleep in another room...': stay in your bed with interceptor traps under each leg.

how-to-get-rid-of-carpet-beetles.label: To store fabrics sealed
how-to-get-rid-of-carpet-beetles.name: Airtight plastic storage bins
how-to-get-rid-of-carpet-beetles.basis: Quick answer: clean, freeze or discard what the larvae eat, vacuum edges and vents, 'and store fabrics sealed, as the University of Kentucky advises'; 'How do you get rid of carpet beetles?': 'Store clean items sealed in tight-fitting plastic bags or containers (Kentucky)'; closets are generally not airtight (UC IPM).

how-to-get-rid-of-cockroaches.label: To bait hiding places
how-to-get-rid-of-cockroaches.name: Cockroach gel bait
how-to-get-rid-of-cockroaches.basis: 'Step 3: Put bait where they hide': 'Gel bait beside the hiding places does most of the killing'; Rutgers says gel usually beats stations because it goes closer to the roaches; use many pea-sized dots (Kentucky) and follow the label. The page also says to trust trap counts, since store-bought baits varied in one apartment study.

how-to-get-rid-of-earwigs.label: To seal door gaps
how-to-get-rid-of-earwigs.name: Door weather stripping
how-to-get-rid-of-earwigs.basis: 'How do you get rid of earwigs in the house?': 'Colorado State says earwigs usually get in through small gaps along doors, windows and vents, which can be sealed with caulk, and Wisconsin adds putty and weather stripping around doors and windows'; quick answer: seal gaps. Indoor insecticides are not recommended (UC IPM).

how-to-get-rid-of-fleas.label: To comb fleas off pets
how-to-get-rid-of-fleas.name: Fine-toothed flea comb
how-to-get-rid-of-fleas.basis: 'How do you treat fleas on dogs and cats?': 'A soap bath and a flea comb deal with the adults on the animal', and the CDC recommends combing afterward with attention to the face, neck and the area in front of the tail; 'How do you get rid of fleas?': confirm it is fleas by combing the pet over a white sink.

how-to-get-rid-of-fungus-gnats.label: To trap the adults
how-to-get-rid-of-fungus-gnats.name: Yellow sticky traps
how-to-get-rid-of-fungus-gnats.basis: Quick answer: trap the adults on yellow sticky cards; '2. Yellow Sticky Traps': Colorado State says to place yellow sticky cards under the plant canopy or on the edge of the container, which may help by mass-trapping adult females; Bti does not affect adults, so sticky traps are needed for the fliers.

how-to-get-rid-of-gnats.label: To catch and identify gnats
how-to-get-rid-of-gnats.name: Yellow sticky traps
how-to-get-rid-of-gnats.basis: 'How can you tell which gnat you have?': 'Catch a few on a yellow sticky card or a strip of clear tape and look at them with a magnifying glass'; 'How do you get rid of gnats in houseplants?': yellow sticky cards under the leaves or along the pot rim catch the adults (Colorado State); vinegar traps do not work for fungus gnats.

how-to-get-rid-of-mice-humanely.label: To seal mice out
how-to-get-rid-of-mice-humanely.name: Steel wool for mouse holes
how-to-get-rid-of-mice-humanely.basis: Quick answer: 'The most humane way to get rid of mice is to seal every gap larger than 1/4 inch so they cannot get in'; HowTo step 'Seal small holes': 'Pack steel wool into holes about the width of a pencil and put caulk around it' (CDC); the page notes a steel wool plug is checked and replaced when it rusts.

how-to-get-rid-of-mosquitoes.label: For water you cannot empty
how-to-get-rid-of-mosquitoes.name: Bti larvicide dunks
how-to-get-rid-of-mosquitoes.basis: Quick answer: 'treat water you cannot empty with a larvicide such as Bti'; 'How do you treat water you cannot empty?': CDC says homeowners can use dunks or bits containing larvicide in small bodies of water that will not be used for drinking; UC IPM says the dunk lasts about 30 days; do not apply more than the label directs (CDC).

how-to-get-rid-of-silverfish.label: To dry the air
how-to-get-rid-of-silverfish.name: Dehumidifier
how-to-get-rid-of-silverfish.basis: Quick answer: you get rid of silverfish 'by drying the air'; H1 'Humidity First, Then Baits and Dusts'; 'How do you get rid of silverfish, step by step?': UC IPM says silverfish require a lot of moisture, so dehumidifiers in closed spaces can help discourage them; EPA's indoor target is 30 to 50 percent humidity.

how-to-get-rid-of-stink-bugs.label: To seal gaps before fall
how-to-get-rid-of-stink-bugs.name: Silicone caulk
how-to-get-rid-of-stink-bugs.basis: Quick answer: Penn State Extension calls sealing the best way to keep stink bugs out; 'How do you keep stink bugs out of the house?': 'Caulk cracks around windows, doors, siding, pipes and wires, behind chimneys and under fascia and soffits, using good-quality silicone or silicone-latex caulk (Penn State)'. Indoor sprays and foggers are not recommended.

how-to-keep-mosquitoes-away.label: For exposed skin
how-to-keep-mosquitoes-away.name: Picaridin insect repellent
how-to-keep-mosquitoes-away.basis: Quick answer: put an EPA-registered repellent on exposed skin; 'Which mosquito repellent should you choose?': choose a product with an EPA registration number and one of CDC's six active ingredients, picaridin among them, which the Yellow Book says can be used on children without age restriction. Use as the label directs.

kissing-bug-look-alikes.label: To contain one for ID
kissing-bug-look-alikes.name: Clear specimen jars with lids
kissing-bug-look-alikes.basis: 'What should you do if you find a kissing bug?': collect it without bare hands, 'then keep the bug in a closed plastic bag, a vial or another small container', freeze it and send photos for identification (Texas A&M Kissing Bug program); Texas DSHS asks for no alcohol or preservatives in the container.

lawn-pest-control.label: For lawn fire ants
lawn-pest-control.name: Fire ant bait granules
lawn-pest-control.basis: 'How do you get rid of fire ants in a lawn?': 'Broadcast bait across the yard first, then treat the mounds that remain'; Texas A&M: broadcast between late August and mid-October, use fresh bait from an unopened container, expect weeks to months to reach 80 to 90 percent control; use bait as its label directs.

mice-exterminator.label: If it is one mouse
mice-exterminator.name: Mouse snap traps
mice-exterminator.basis: FAQ 'Is it worth calling an exterminator for one mouse?': 'Set several snap traps against walls near the sighting and check them daily'; 'What does an exterminator do for mice?': Nebraska calls trapping the preferred method in homes and the CDC recommends traditional snap traps.

mice-poison.label: To try before poison
mice-poison.name: Mouse snap traps
mice-poison.basis: Quick answer: University of California guidance treats trapping as the first step; 'Bromethalin or an anticoagulant': 'A snap trap raises none of these questions, which is the case for starting with mouse traps'; FAQ: in a home with pets, traps set where the pet cannot reach avoid the poison question. No rodenticide picked.

mice-removal.label: To trap mice inside
mice-removal.name: Mouse snap traps
mice-removal.basis: Quick answer: seal every opening 1/4 inch or larger, 'trap the mice already inside with snap traps', and clean up wet; HowTo step 'Set snap traps': bait with a small amount of chunky peanut butter, baited end against the wall, no more than about 10 feet apart (CDC, Nebraska).

mice-repellent.label: To remove resident mice
mice-repellent.name: Mouse snap traps
mice-repellent.basis: Quick answer: 'Closing gaps and trapping are the steps the sources support'; 'What works instead of a repellent?', subsection 'Set traps where the mice are active': NC State says to set snap traps along mouse runways, out of reach of children and pets; UC IPM spaces traps no more than about 10 feet apart.

mice-traps.label: To trap house mice
mice-traps.name: Mouse snap traps
mice-traps.basis: Quick answer: 'For most homes, a traditional snap trap is the right mouse trap. The CDC recommends snap traps and says not to use glue traps or live traps'; HowTo step 'Pick the right trap': buy mouse-size traditional snap traps with a wide trigger plate.

millipedes.label: To seal the door gap
millipedes.name: Door sweep
millipedes.basis: 'How do you get rid of millipedes in the house?': 'Kentucky names door thresholds and windowsills as possible entry points and suggests caulking gaps and fitting door sweeps or weather stripping'; FAQ 'Can millipedes climb walls?' repeats it. Pesticides are rarely justified (UC IPM, Kentucky).

moths-in-house.label: To monitor pantry moths
moths-in-house.name: Pantry moth pheromone traps
moths-in-house.basis: 'How do you get rid of pantry moths?': 'Pheromone traps for Indian meal moths catch the males and show whether moths remain after the cleanup; UC IPM says to check them weekly'; FAQ 'Will moth traps get rid of moths?': they detect an infestation and give some control, alongside cleaning. Label limits it to pantry moths.

mouse-poop.label: For droppings cleanup
mouse-poop.name: Disposable gloves
mouse-poop.basis: 'How do you clean up mouse droppings safely?': CDC step 'Put on rubber or plastic gloves.'

natural-garden-pest-control.label: To shield young plants
natural-garden-pest-control.name: Floating row cover
natural-garden-pest-control.basis: 'What order should natural garden pest control follow?': 'Floating row covers keep some adult insects from laying eggs on new plants but have to come off for pollination'; 'When should you stop and try something else?': move to hand removal, water or row covers.

natural-pest-control.label: To seal small gaps first
natural-pest-control.name: Steel wool for mouse holes
natural-pest-control.basis: Quick answer: natural pest control starts by sealing entry points; bullet: mice fit through a 1/4-inch hole, 'which is why sealing gaps with steel wool and caulk comes before any spray'; 'Where should natural pest control start?': fill small holes with steel wool and put caulk around it (CDC).

natural-weed-control.label: To pull whole taproots
natural-weed-control.name: Fishtail hand weeder
natural-weed-control.basis: '3. Pull after rain': the University of California suggests a dandelion fork or fishtail weeder for weeds with a thick taproot; HowTo step and cheat sheet: 'lever out the whole taproot with a fishtail weeder before the weed sets seed'.

palmetto-bugs.label: To seal cracks they use
palmetto-bugs.name: Exterior caulk
palmetto-bugs.basis: 'What should you do once you know which one it is?': 'UF recommends caulking cracks around door and window frames and around plumbing and electrical lines, weather-stripping doors and repairing window and soffit screens'; quick answer bullet: one big roach indoors is usually a stray, and UF says removing outdoor cockroaches is often all the control needed.

pantry-pests.label: To store dry goods
pantry-pests.name: Airtight food storage containers
pantry-pests.basis: 'How do you keep pantry pests from coming back?': Minnesota Extension recommends storing food in tightly closed glass, metal or heavy plastic containers; UC IPM says plastic bags are not adequate; FAQ 'Can bugs get into sealed packages?': tightly closed glass, metal or heavy plastic containers are what the extension guides recommend.

peppermint-oil-for-mice.label: To seal holes instead
peppermint-oil-for-mice.name: Steel wool for mouse holes
peppermint-oil-for-mice.basis: Quick answer: CDC and University of California guidance rely on sealing, sanitation and trapping, not peppermint oil; 'Where does peppermint oil fit in a real mouse control plan?': fill small holes with steel wool with caulk around it (CDC); FAQ 'What works better than peppermint oil for mice?' lists steel wool and caulk.

pet-safe-pest-control.label: Instead of mouse poison
pet-safe-pest-control.name: Mouse snap traps
pet-safe-pest-control.basis: Quick answer: 'set traps where paws cannot reach'; 'Which pest products are most dangerous to cats and dogs?': rat and mouse poison causes the most pet poisonings and 'A snap trap leaves no bait and no poisoned carcass'; risk table lists snap traps as the alternative to rat and mouse poison.

raccoon-poop.label: For latrine cleanup
raccoon-poop.name: Disposable gloves
raccoon-poop.basis: 'How do you clean up raccoon poop safely?': 'Put on disposable gloves, and rubber boots you can scrub or disposable shoe covers'; FAQ 'What should I do if I find raccoon poop in my yard?': wear disposable gloves and scrubbable boots, mist the pile, bag it and treat hard surfaces with boiling water.

rat-droppings.label: To trap rats
rat-droppings.name: Rat-size snap traps
rat-droppings.basis: 'What should you do once you know it is rats?': CDC recommends traditional snap traps, not glue or live traps, and NC State Extension adds that mouse snap traps are typically not an effective tool against rats; FAQ 'What should I do if I find rat droppings?': after cleanup, seal entry gaps and set snap traps.

rat-vs-mouse.label: For cleanup after rodents
rat-vs-mouse.name: Disposable gloves
rat-vs-mouse.basis: 'What should you do once you know which one it is?': CDC cleanup step 'Put on rubber or plastic gloves.'

red-ants.label: For fire ant mounds
red-ants.name: Fire ant bait granules
red-ants.basis: 'How do you get rid of fire ants?': 'Bait first: broadcast a fire ant bait across the yard, then treat individual problem mounds' (Texas A&M Two-Step Method); California's guide does not recommend products not labeled as fire ant baits; use fresh bait, as the label directs.

roof-rat-vs-norway-rat.label: To trap either rat
roof-rat-vs-norway-rat.name: Rat-size snap traps
roof-rat-vs-norway-rat.basis: 'What should you do once you know which rat it is?': let the species decide where traps go; UC IPM says to set traps for Norway rats close to walls, behind objects and in dark corners, and for roof rats both on the ground and above it on ledges, shelves, branches, fences, pipes or beams.

seed-ticks.label: To lift off seed ticks
seed-ticks.name: Duct tape
seed-ticks.basis: Quick answer: the University of Rhode Island's TickEncounter program 'recommends lifting loose larvae off with duct tape before they attach'; 'How do you remove dozens of seed ticks at once?': use tape, not tweezers, for the loose ones; URI calls duct tape a very effective way to de-tick and lint rollers less sticky.

signs-of-bed-bugs-checklist.label: For the 10-minute check
signs-of-bed-bugs-checklist.name: LED flashlight
signs-of-bed-bugs-checklist.basis: 'How do you check for bed bugs tonight in 10 minutes?': 'Work outward from the pillow with a flashlight and a stiff card, because that is where the evidence concentrates'; FAQ 'Do I have to check for bed bugs at night?': a daytime check with a flashlight along the seams, box spring, headboard and frame will find the signs.

spider-egg-sacs.label: For egg sac removal
spider-egg-sacs.name: Leather work gloves
spider-egg-sacs.basis: 'What should you do with a spider egg sac?': 'Kansas State advises leather gloves, long sleeves and long pants, and removing the spiders, webbing and all egg sacs with a broom or other long-handled tool, or a vacuum'. Sprays and fogs are not effective on sacs (UC IPM, UMN).

spiders-in-california.label: For clearing garage clutter
spiders-in-california.name: Work gloves
spiders-in-california.basis: 'What should you do about spiders around a California home?': 'Garages. Wear gloves when clearing clutter'

spiders-in-florida.label: For woodpiles and storage
spiders-in-florida.name: Work gloves
spiders-in-florida.basis: 'What should you do about spiders around a Florida home?': 'Wear gloves when lifting boards or firewood or reaching into storage boxes' (FDACS pest alert), and wear gloves in sheds, basements and attics, as UF's black widow profile suggests.

spiders-in-texas.label: For stored items
spiders-in-texas.name: Lidded plastic storage bins
spiders-in-texas.basis: 'What should you do about spiders and spider bites in Texas?': 'Texas A&M suggests taping stored boxes shut or using lidded plastic bins, and moving firewood away from the house'; also wear gloves where spiders live and shake out stored shoes, clothes and towels.

steel-wool-for-mice.label: To plug small holes
steel-wool-for-mice.name: Coarse steel wool
steel-wool-for-mice.basis: Quick answer: the CDC says to fill small holes with steel wool and put caulk around it; 'What kind of steel wool should you use?': 'The practical reading is to buy the coarsest plain steel wool on the shelf'; for openings up to about 3/4 inch, with hardware cloth, sheet metal or concrete for larger ones.

sugar-ants.label: To bait the trail
sugar-ants.name: Liquid ant bait stations
sugar-ants.basis: Quick answer: 'use a slow-acting bait and skip the spray'; HowTo step 'Set slow-acting bait beside the trail': 'Place a bait station next to the trail where pets and small children cannot reach it. Start with a sweet bait'; Kentucky recommends syrupy, sweet baits for odorous house ants.

termite-damage.label: To save wings for ID
termite-damage.name: Clear specimen jars with lids
termite-damage.basis: The page sends treatment to a licensed professional and says to skip the spray can. Neutral identification aid from its own method, callout 'Bring the evidence': photograph damage beside a ruler 'and keep a few insects or wings in a sealed jar' for the extension office or inspector to identify.

termite-droppings.label: To see the six sides
termite-droppings.name: Magnifying glass
termite-droppings.basis: Quick answer bullet: Texas A&M says drywood termite pellets have lengthwise flutes 'that show under magnification'; 'What do termite droppings look like?': the flutes show under modest magnification; UC IPM calls six-sided pellets diagnostic for drywood termites.

tick-identification-chart.label: To save a removed tick
tick-identification-chart.name: Small plastic specimen vials
tick-identification-chart.basis: 'What should you do with a tick you have removed, and how do you get it identified?': 'the Connecticut handbook says a sealable plastic bag will do, although a small plastic vial is best, and that rubbing alcohol will preserve a tick'; tick-check routine: seal the tick in a bag or vial and note the date and place.

ticks-by-state.label: To remove a tick
ticks-by-state.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-by-state.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite?': 'Take the tick off with clean, fine-tipped tweezers, grasping it as close to the skin as possible and pulling it away with steady, even pressure, without twisting or jerking'.

ticks-in-alabama.label: For clothing and gear
ticks-in-alabama.name: Permethrin clothing spray (0.5%)
ticks-in-alabama.basis: 'How do you prevent tick bites in Alabama?': 'The department recommends 0.5% permethrin on clothes, and Alabama Extension calls treating clothing and gear the most effective preventive step when used according to the label.' Clothing and gear only, per the label.

ticks-in-arkansas.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-arkansas.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-arkansas.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Arkansas?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin as possible with clean, fine-tipped tweezers.'

ticks-in-connecticut.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-connecticut.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-connecticut.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Connecticut?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin as you can, with fine-tipped tweezers if you have them.'

ticks-in-delaware.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-delaware.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-delaware.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Delaware?': 'Grasp the tick with clean, fine-tipped tweezers as close to the skin's surface as possible.'

ticks-in-georgia.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-georgia.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-georgia.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Georgia?': 'Grasp the tick with clean, fine-tipped tweezers as close to the skin's surface as possible.'

ticks-in-illinois.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-illinois.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-illinois.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Illinois?': 'Grasp the tick with fine-tipped tweezers as close to the skin's surface as possible.'

ticks-in-indiana.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-indiana.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-indiana.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Indiana?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible with clean, fine-tipped tweezers.'

ticks-in-kentucky.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-kentucky.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-kentucky.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Kentucky?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible using clean, fine-tipped tweezers.'

ticks-in-maine.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-maine.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-maine.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Maine?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible with clean, fine-tipped tweezers.'

ticks-in-maryland.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-maryland.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-maryland.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Maryland?': 'Grasp the tick with fine-tipped tweezers or forceps as close to the skin as possible'; FAQ on the Asian longhorned tick: remove an attached tick with fine-tipped tweezers, then mail it to a state identification service.

ticks-in-massachusetts.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-massachusetts.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-massachusetts.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Massachusetts?': 'Grip the tick with fine-point tweezers as close to the skin as possible.'; FAQ 'How long does a tick have to be attached...': remove any attached tick right away with fine-point tweezers.

ticks-in-michigan.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-michigan.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-michigan.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Michigan?': 'Remove the tick promptly with fine-tipped tweezers'; 'Grasp the tick with fine-tipped tweezers or a tick removal tool as close to the skin as possible.'

ticks-in-minnesota.label: For clothing and gear
ticks-in-minnesota.name: Permethrin clothing spray (0.5%)
ticks-in-minnesota.basis: 'How do you prevent tick bites in Minnesota?': 'MDH especially recommends permethrin products on clothing and gear for people who spend a lot of time in wooded areas, and never on skin.'

ticks-in-mississippi.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-mississippi.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-mississippi.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Mississippi?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible with clean, fine-tipped tweezers'.

ticks-in-missouri.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-missouri.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-missouri.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Missouri?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible with clean, fine-tipped tweezers.'

ticks-in-new-hampshire.label: For clothing and gear
ticks-in-new-hampshire.name: Permethrin clothing spray (0.5%)
ticks-in-new-hampshire.basis: 'How do you prevent tick bites in New Hampshire?': 'Use permethrin on clothing, not skin. The state calls permethrin highly effective at repelling ticks on clothing and says it is not meant for skin; CDC recommends clothing and gear treated with 0.5% permethrin.'

ticks-in-new-jersey.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-new-jersey.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-new-jersey.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in New Jersey?': 'Grasp the tick with fine-tipped tweezers as close to the skin as possible.'

ticks-in-new-york.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-new-york.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-new-york.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in New York?': 'Use pointed tweezers and grasp the tick by the head or mouth, right where it enters the skin, not by its body.'

ticks-in-north-carolina.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-north-carolina.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-north-carolina.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in North Carolina?': 'Use clean, fine-tipped tweezers to grip the tick as close to the skin as you can.'

ticks-in-ohio.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-ohio.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-ohio.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Ohio?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible with clean, fine-tipped tweezers.'

ticks-in-oklahoma.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-oklahoma.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-oklahoma.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Oklahoma?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible with clean, fine-tipped tweezers.'

ticks-in-pennsylvania.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-pennsylvania.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-pennsylvania.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Pennsylvania?': 'Grasp the tick with fine-tipped tweezers as close to the skin as possible.'; the Asian longhorned tick section adds fine-point tweezers for pets and farm animals.

ticks-in-rhode-island.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-rhode-island.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-rhode-island.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Rhode Island?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible with clean, fine-tipped tweezers.'; FAQ 'Should I see a doctor after a tick bite...': remove the tick right away with fine-tipped tweezers.

ticks-in-south-carolina.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-south-carolina.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-south-carolina.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in South Carolina?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin as you can with clean, fine-tipped tweezers.'

ticks-in-tennessee.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-tennessee.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-tennessee.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Tennessee?': 'Grasp the tick with tweezers as close to the skin as possible and pull straight out, without using bare hands.'

ticks-in-texas.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-texas.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-texas.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Texas?': 'Use tweezers or forceps; if you use your fingers, wear disposable gloves or shield them with a paper towel.'

ticks-in-vermont.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-vermont.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-vermont.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Vermont?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible with clean, fine-tipped tweezers.'

ticks-in-virginia.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-virginia.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-virginia.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Virginia?': 'Grasp the tick with tweezers as close to the skin as possible.'

ticks-in-west-virginia.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-west-virginia.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-west-virginia.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in West Virginia?': 'Grip the tick with clean, fine-tipped tweezers as close to the skin as you can.'; FAQ on the Asian longhorned tick: remove an attached tick with fine-tipped tweezers and keep it.

ticks-in-wisconsin.label: To remove a tick
ticks-in-wisconsin.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-in-wisconsin.basis: 'What should you do after a tick bite in Wisconsin?': 'Grasp the tick with narrow-bladed tweezers as close to the skin as possible; if you have none, cover your fingers with tissue paper or rubber gloves.'

ticks-on-dogs.label: To pull ticks off dogs
ticks-on-dogs.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-on-dogs.basis: Quick answer: 'pull any attached tick straight out with fine-tipped tweezers as soon as you find it'; 'How do you remove a tick from a dog?': grasp the tick with fine-tipped tweezers as close to the skin as you can, the method in CAPC's guidelines, which also say to wear gloves. Prescription preventives were not picked.

ticks-that-carry-lyme-disease.label: To remove a tick
ticks-that-carry-lyme-disease.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
ticks-that-carry-lyme-disease.basis: 'What should you do after a bite from a tick that may carry Lyme disease?': 'Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible with clean fine-tipped tweezers'; if you have none, CDC says regular tweezers or fingers; keep the tick in a sealed container or rubbing alcohol.

tiny-ants.label: To count the waist nodes
tiny-ants.name: Magnifying glass
tiny-ants.basis: 'How do you identify a tiny ant?': 'With a magnifier or a phone camera zoomed in, count the small knobs, called nodes, in the narrow waist'; FAQ 'What is the tiny yellow ant in my kitchen?': the right bait differs by species, 'so a close look with a magnifier is worth the effort'.

tiny-black-bugs.label: To check tiny bugs
tiny-black-bugs.name: Magnifying glass
tiny-black-bugs.basis: 'How do you tell which tiny black bug you have?': catch one in a clear jar or on clear tape; 'A magnifying glass helps: many of these insects are 1/8 inch long or less'; under a magnifier, fleas, flour beetles and most spider beetles turn out reddish brown.

tiny-brown-bugs.label: To check tiny bugs
tiny-brown-bugs.name: Magnifying glass
tiny-brown-bugs.basis: 'How do you tell which tiny brown bug you have?': 'Catch one in a clear jar or press it onto clear tape, then look at it with a magnifying glass, because many of these are 1/8 inch long or less.'

types-of-mice.label: For cleaning up after mice
types-of-mice.name: Disposable nitrile gloves
types-of-mice.basis: 'Which types of mice carry hantavirus?': callout: 'wear nonfabric gloves (rubber, latex, vinyl or nitrile)'

vamoose-for-mice.label: To seal entry points
vamoose-for-mice.name: Steel wool for mouse holes
vamoose-for-mice.basis: Quick answer: treat a pouch as an optional extra to sealing and trapping; 'What should you pair with Vamoose to get rid of mice?', subsection 'Seal the entry points': CDC says to fill small holes with steel wool and put caulk around it. No scent repellent picked (the page calls the evidence inconsistent).

venomous-spiders.label: To check a spider's eyes
venomous-spiders.name: Magnifying glass
venomous-spiders.basis: 'How do you check a spider you have caught?': trap it in a jar and 'Use a magnifying glass' for the five checks; 'How do you recognize a brown recluse?': you will likely need a hand lens to see the eyes, the University of Arizona notes.

water-bugs-vs-cockroaches.label: To bait where they live
water-bugs-vs-cockroaches.name: Cockroach bait stations
water-bugs-vs-cockroaches.basis: 'How do you get rid of the cockroaches called water bugs?': 'Cut off water, close the gaps, and put bait where the roaches live'; Penn State lists bait active ingredients placed where roaches harbor, and UC IPM recommends placing baits in water meter boxes, drains or under concrete slabs for outdoor-living roaches.

what-do-ants-eat.label: To offer ants a bait
what-do-ants-eat.name: Ant bait stations
what-do-ants-eat.basis: 'Why does what ants eat decide which bait works?': UC recommends setting out a small amount of each kind of bait, 'or several formulations in one bait station', and watching which the ants prefer; FAQ 'Why are ants ignoring my bait?': reposition stations or try another product.

what-do-baby-cockroaches-look-like.label: For many small placements
what-do-baby-cockroaches-look-like.name: Cockroach gel bait
what-do-baby-cockroaches-look-like.basis: 'What should you do after finding baby cockroaches?': 'Use bait in many small placements'; Texas A&M calls baits among the most effective insecticides for cockroaches in homes and says many small, pea-sized gel placements work better than a few large ones; skip bug bombs.

what-do-bed-bugs-look-like.label: To check seams for eggs
what-do-bed-bugs-look-like.name: Lighted magnifying glass
what-do-bed-bugs-look-like.basis: 'What do bed bug eggs look like?', callout 'Use magnification': 'Check seams with a magnifying glass and strong light before deciding a mattress is clear'; the University of Kentucky says the eggs are hard to see without magnification.

what-do-fleas-look-like.label: To see fleas up close
what-do-fleas-look-like.name: Magnifying glass
what-do-fleas-look-like.basis: 'What does a flea look like to the naked eye?': 'The features that set a flea apart show best under a magnifying glass'; 'What does a flea look like under a magnifying glass?': a hard, side-flattened body with backward bristles, and cat and dog fleas show two combs of spines.

what-do-mice-eat.label: To keep food from mice
what-do-mice-eat.name: Airtight food storage containers
what-do-mice-eat.basis: 'How do you store food so mice cannot get it?': 'Seal food in thick plastic, metal or glass containers with tight lids, because thin packaging does not stop a mouse'; good sanitation also makes traps work better by reducing competing food (Timm).

what-do-ticks-look-like.label: To remove a tick
what-do-ticks-look-like.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
what-do-ticks-look-like.basis: 'What should you do after finding a tick?': 'Remove an attached tick with tweezers, then decide whether you want it identified'; Iowa State describes grasping the tick's mouthparts where they enter the skin and pulling steadily, directly away from the skin.

what-kills-ticks-on-dogs-instantly.label: To remove a tick now
what-kills-ticks-on-dogs-instantly.name: Fine-tipped tweezers
what-kills-ticks-on-dogs-instantly.basis: Quick answer: nothing safe kills an attached tick instantly; 'The fastest fix is to pull the tick out with fine-tipped tweezers, following CDC's tick removal steps'; table: fine-tipped tweezers work right away; FAQ on dish soap: pulling the tick with fine-tipped tweezers is quicker. Prescription chews and spot-ons not picked.

what-kills-ticks.label: For clothing and gear
what-kills-ticks.name: Permethrin clothing spray (0.5%)
what-kills-ticks.basis: Quick answer: CDC advises 'treating clothing and gear with 0.5% permethrin'; 'What kills ticks on boots, packs and camping gear?': permethrin applied to fabric kills ticks that crawl across it and stays protective through several washings (CDC); apply it to clothing or other fabrics, never to skin.

what-smells-do-mice-hate.label: To seal gaps instead
what-smells-do-mice-hate.name: Copper mesh for gaps
what-smells-do-mice-hate.basis: Quick answer: sealing gaps, trapping and removing food and shelter are what the guidance describes instead of smells; 'What works better than a smell?': CDC steel wool with caulk for small holes, and 'Copper mesh does not rust, NC State says, but it should also be caulked because rodents can push it aside.'

where-do-bed-bugs-hide.label: To inspect dim corners
where-do-bed-bugs-hide.name: LED flashlight
where-do-bed-bugs-hide.basis: 'How do you inspect a bedroom for bed bugs?': 'Flashlight. Kentucky calls a flashlight useful for dimly lit areas'; 'How do you check a hotel room for bed bugs?': the University of Kentucky's advice for travelers is to inspect beds with a flashlight for dimly lit areas.

where-do-cockroaches-come-from.label: To seal pipe gaps
where-do-cockroaches-come-from.name: Copper mesh for gaps
where-do-cockroaches-come-from.basis: 'How do cockroaches spread between apartments?': Kentucky recommends sealing the openings where plumbing pipes or wires pass through walls or floors with caulk, foam or copper mesh, especially in apartments; the table 'How do you close each route?' and FAQ 'Where do cockroaches come from in an apartment?' repeat it.

whitefly-identification-control.label: For leaf undersides
whitefly-identification-control.name: Insecticidal soap concentrate
whitefly-identification-control.basis: Quick answer: wet the undersides of the leaves with insecticidal soap or oil and repeat every 5 to 7 days; 'Insecticidal soap is the first spray to reach for'; 'Use a commercial insecticidal soap, not a kitchen mix' (Clemson). Spray in the evening, below 90 degrees F, keeping it off open flowers.

wolf-spiders.label: To spot eyeshine at night
wolf-spiders.name: LED flashlight
wolf-spiders.basis: 'What do a wolf spider's eyes look like?': 'Hold a flashlight beside your head at night and their eyes shine back like a cat's, MDC says, and UC IPM says they reflect green'; Texas A&M says a flashlight shone into grass shows dozens of points of light from wolf spiders' eyes.

mouse-urine.label: To check for urine stains
mouse-urine.name: UV flashlight (black light)
mouse-urine.basis: 'Does mouse urine glow under a black light?': the National Park Service says a UV light helps confirm mice when other signs are present as well (Conserve O Gram 3/12).

squirrel-poop.label: For droppings cleanup
squirrel-poop.name: Disposable gloves
squirrel-poop.basis: 'How do you clean up squirrel droppings safely?': CDC step 2, after airing out, 'Put on rubber or plastic gloves.'; FAQ 'Is it safe to clean up squirrel droppings yourself?': 'wear rubber or plastic gloves'

signs-of-carpet-beetles.label: For checking under furniture
signs-of-carpet-beetles.name: LED flashlight
signs-of-carpet-beetles.basis: 'Take a flashlight, as Ohio State suggests for checking under baseboards and furniture.'

signs-of-cockroaches.label: To confirm and count roaches
signs-of-cockroaches.name: Cockroach sticky traps
signs-of-cockroaches.basis: 'How do you confirm a cockroach infestation, and how bad is it?': 'Set sticky traps: they catch roaches you never see and show where most of them are.'

oriental-cockroaches.label: To see if more roaches turn up
oriental-cockroaches.name: Cockroach sticky traps
oriental-cockroaches.basis: 'How can you tell if you have Oriental cockroaches?': 'let sticky traps do the counting'; FAQ 'Should I worry if I see one Oriental cockroach?': set sticky traps near drains, doors and damp spots 'to see whether more turn up'

white-cockroach.label: To check for more roaches
white-cockroach.name: Cockroach sticky traps
white-cockroach.basis: 'UC IPM calls sticky traps the best way to detect and monitor cockroaches: put them where floors meet walls near the spot and check them daily for several days.'

bed-bug-bites-but-no-bed-bugs.label: To catch bed bugs at the bed legs
bed-bug-bites-but-no-bed-bugs.name: Bed bug interceptor cups
bed-bug-bites-but-no-bed-bugs.basis: Kentucky's bed bug fact sheet: interceptor traps, small dishes under bed and furniture legs that wandering bed bugs fall into; checked regularly they can reveal an infestation early.

brown-banded-cockroaches.label: To find where they hide
brown-banded-cockroaches.name: Cockroach sticky traps
brown-banded-cockroaches.basis: 'Set sticky traps against walls and in corners of floors, shelves and drawers at ten or more spots for a week, as Penn State advises', to find where brown-banded cockroaches hide (they live and breed entirely indoors, per UC IPM).

mice-in-walls.label: To catch mice leaving the wall
mice-in-walls.name: Mouse snap traps
mice-in-walls.basis: 'Set snap traps there, flat on the floor with the baited end touching the wall so trap and wall form a T, with a little chunky peanut butter on the bait pan, as CDC advises': trap where mice leave the wall, then seal after a week with no catches.

camel-crickets.label: To dry out the basement
camel-crickets.name: Dehumidifier
camel-crickets.basis: 'Maryland Extension says solving high moisture problems in a basement will greatly reduce or eliminate camel crickets': dry the space and seal the way in before any insecticide (the page also names sticky boards, NC State and Clemson).

flea-dirt.label: To check your pet for flea dirt
flea-dirt.name: Fine-toothed flea comb
flea-dirt.basis: 'Comb over something white. Stand the pet in a white sink or tub (Ohio State) or on white paper or a pillowcase (Cornell) and run a fine-toothed flea comb through the coat.'

bed-bugs-in-hotels.label: To check the hotel room
bed-bugs-in-hotels.name: Small LED flashlight
bed-bugs-in-hotels.basis: 'set your luggage on a counter or another hard surface, then shine a flashlight along the mattress seams, piping and tags at the pillow end'; the room checklist says 'Run a flashlight along every seam at the head of the bed' (EPA, Kentucky).

daddy-long-legs.label: To clear the webs
daddy-long-legs.name: Extendable cobweb duster
daddy-long-legs.basis: The page advises tolerating cellar spiders when possible and 'removing webs and egg sacs with a broom or vacuum' (Minnesota Extension, UC IPM); a long-handled web duster reaches the ceiling corners where their webs hang. Never an insecticide.

yellow-sac-spiders.label: To see where they roam
yellow-sac-spiders.name: Sticky traps
yellow-sac-spiders.basis: 'Check with sticky traps': 'Minnesota says sticky traps along walls and under furniture show whether spiders are present' (also UC IPM).

springtails.label: To dry out damp rooms
springtails.name: Dehumidifier
springtails.basis: 'Penn State calls air conditioning or a dehumidifier the best way to manage springtails indoors, especially in bathrooms and showers'; the page puts moisture first and recommends no insecticide.

joro-spiders.label: To take down a web
joro-spiders.name: Extendable cobweb duster
joro-spiders.basis: 'Where a web blocks a path, porch, deck or doorway, UGA suggests using a broom, rake, long stick or pole to wrap the spider in its web and take it away'; the page passes on UGA's advice against spraying insecticides over large areas. Never an insecticide.

jumping-spiders.label: To catch it and let it go
jumping-spiders.name: Clear plastic jar with lid
jumping-spiders.basis: 'UC IPM describes the same catch, setting a jar over the spider, sliding a piece of paper underneath and releasing it outdoors'; the ID tip says 'Trap the spider under a clear jar'. Never an insecticide.

camel-spiders.label: To trap it and let it go
camel-spiders.name: Clear plastic jar with lid
camel-spiders.basis: 'To remove one, UC IPM says to trap it under a jar, slide paper underneath and release it outdoors; it recommends no chemical control'. Never an insecticide.

what-do-termites-look-like.label: To save a sample for an expert
what-do-termites-look-like.name: Small specimen jars
what-do-termites-look-like.basis: "drop a few termites, soldiers or swarmers if you can find them, into a small jar of alcohol"; "For a sure answer, save a few in alcohol ... for an extension office or a licensed inspector" (Mississippi State suggests preserving swarmers in alcohol for identification). Never an insecticide.

orb-weaver-spiders.label: To draw fewer bugs to the door
orb-weaver-spiders.name: Yellow bug light bulbs
orb-weaver-spiders.basis: "UC IPM suggests keeping light fixtures off the house and away from windows and doors where possible; Minnesota suggests yellow bulbs, which draw fewer insects" (orb weavers build where lights draw their prey). Never an insecticide.

carpet-beetle-larvae.label: To vacuum vents and rug edges
carpet-beetle-larvae.name: Cordless handheld vacuum
carpet-beetle-larvae.basis: "Kentucky says to launder, dry-clean or discard infested items ... and to vacuum floors, carpets and heating vents"; the hiding-places list names rug edges, baseboards, vents and ducts (Kentucky, Ohio State). Never an insecticide.

weevils.label: To keep grains sealed
weevils.name: Airtight food storage containers
weevils.basis: "**Store food sealed** in tightly closed glass, metal or heavy plastic containers, or in the refrigerator or freezer, until the infestation is gone (UMN, Iowa State)". Not a moth trap: the page says pheromone traps for the Indian meal moth will not catch weevils (UC IPM). Never an insecticide.

shrews.label: To cover entry points
shrews.name: 1/4-inch hardware cloth
shrews.basis: "The chapter says rodent-proofing keeps shrews out too: cover possible entrances with 1/4-inch hardware cloth and stuff small openings with coarse steel wool" (Prevention and Control of Wildlife Damage, shrew chapter). Never a poison.

pill-bugs.label: To seal the gap under a door
pill-bugs.name: Door sweep
pill-bugs.basis: "**Seal the way in.** UC IPM recommends weather stripping and door sweeps, and Idaho names loose sliding patio doors, basement windows next to window wells and foundation vents as easy ways in". Never an insecticide.

booklice.label: To bring humidity below 50%
booklice.name: Dehumidifier
booklice.basis: "Penn State says keeping relative humidity below 50% prevents mold growth and booklouse development, so a dehumidifier or moisture absorber can be very effective"; DCPH-A: keep the dehumidifier running. Never an insecticide.

mud-daubers.label: To scrape off old nests
mud-daubers.name: Putty knife
mud-daubers.basis: "**Scrape it off.** Purdue says to scrape the nest away with a putty knife and dispose of it, which prevents mud daubers emerging from it the following year". Never an insecticide.

wheel-bugs.label: To keep masked hunters out
wheel-bugs.name: Door sweep
wheel-bugs.basis: "Penn State says the best control is to find and eliminate the pests a masked hunter feeds on ... and Utah State suggests door sweeps on doors leading outside or into a garage, and regular vacuuming". Never an insecticide.

jerusalem-crickets.label: To catch it and let it go
jerusalem-crickets.name: Clear plastic jar with lid
jerusalem-crickets.basis: "**Use a hard container.** Slide a clear jar or a hard plastic container over it, photograph it beside a ruler marked in inches, and note where you found it". Never an insecticide.

paper-wasps.label: For a nest you must remove
paper-wasps.name: Wasp and hornet spray
paper-wasps.basis: "**Use a wasp and hornet spray labeled for nests**"; "Penn State says these sprays shoot a stream up to 20 feet, and Kentucky says most make the insects drop instantly, so never stand under the nest". The page names this type; UF and Utah State's no-spray options are also on the page.

carpet-beetle-rash.label: For itchy skin
carpet-beetle-rash.name: Hydrocortisone cream
carpet-beetle-rash.basis: "**Try an over-the-counter remedy.** MedlinePlus suggests hydrocortisone cream on the itchy areas or an oral antihistamine"; the MedlinePlus list later on the page also names over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream.

pseudoscorpions.label: To dry out a damp room
pseudoscorpions.name: Dehumidifier
pseudoscorpions.basis: "**Dry out damp rooms.** Wisconsin says pseudoscorpions prefer humid conditions in homes, and Penn State's booklice page suggests a dehumidifier, a moisture absorber or another way to bring relative humidity below 50%". Never an insecticide.

possum-vs-opossum.label: To close a den opening
possum-vs-opossum.name: 1/4-inch hardware cloth
possum-vs-opossum.basis: "**Close the gap for good.** Washington recommends 1/4-inch mesh hardware cloth, boards or metal flashing"; the page repeats it: close the opening with hardware cloth once the animal has left.

how-long-do-rats-live.label: For rats in the house
how-long-do-rats-live.name: Rat snap traps
how-long-do-rats-live.basis: "**Set snap traps, not glue or live traps.** CDC's trapping guide recommends traditional snap traps made for rats, set on the floor against the wall, and advises against glue and live traps". Snap traps made for rats, as the page says; never glue or live traps.

deer-poop.label: For picking up droppings
deer-poop.name: Disposable gloves
deer-poop.basis: "keep deer droppings off food, remove them with gloves or a tool and wash your hands afterward" (the CDC E. coli and Salmonella sentence). The page names gloves; nothing else to buy.

maggots.label: To keep flies out of garbage
maggots.name: Outdoor trash can with a tight-fitting lid
maggots.basis: Prevention list: 'Use a tight-fitting lid and keep the can as far from the house as you can' (UC IPM / UMN steps on the page).

dust-mites.label: One part of a several-step plan
dust-mites.name: Zippered dust mite mattress encasement
dust-mites.basis: The page cites the NIH guideline: for people sensitive to dust mites, mite-proof pillow and mattress covers along with a HEPA vacuum, because one strategy alone often does not improve asthma. Label says it is one step of several.

black-widow-spiders.label: For clearing clutter and firewood
black-widow-spiders.name: Heavy-duty work gloves
black-widow-spiders.basis: 'Wear gloves. UC IPM advises gloves when clearing clutter in garages and storage areas, Clemson for firewood' (prevention list).

rabbit-poop.label: For picking up droppings
rabbit-poop.name: Disposable gloves
rabbit-poop.basis: 'So pick droppings up with a shovel or a gloved hand ... and wash your hands' plus Wildlife Illinois' rubber gloves for handling a dead rabbit.

spider-mites.label: To see the mites
spider-mites.name: 10x hand lens magnifier
spider-mites.basis: 'Through a 10X hand lens, UC IPM says, you can see an oval body with eight legs' (identification section).

fleas-on-humans.label: To check your pet for fleas
fleas-on-humans.name: Fine-toothed flea comb
fleas-on-humans.search: flea comb for dogs and cats
fleas-on-humans.basis: Lead photo caption: 'Texas A&M says the fine teeth of a flea comb remove adult fleas from fur.'
